samir: Noticed a subtle difference between sync and async Python SDK tool_call structured_output handling. Sync returns Mapping, async sometimes wraps it into a list. Reduced repro below.

samir: Async repro: 
```py
from redwood_inference import AsyncClient
import asyncio

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key='sk-...')
    resp = await c.tool_call('product_search', {'q': 'sprocket'}, structured_output=True)
    print(type(resp.tool_output))
    print(resp.tool_output)

asyncio.run(main())
```

samir: Raw wire payload we get from the service: `{"id":"req-77","tool_output":{"catalog":{"count":2,"items":[{"id":"a"}]}}}`. Sync prints `<class 'dict'>`, async prints `<class 'list'>` and output becomes `[{...}]`.

leah: which sdk version and python? Any middleware that might wrap responses?

samir: redwood-inference==0.9.4, python 3.11. No middleware on our side.

toni: I can reproduce locally. The problem is in _normalize_structured_output: it checks Sequence before Mapping, so dict-like objects that are also iterable can get misclassified. Swapping the checks or explicitly checking Mapping first fixes it.

leah: good catch. We should also add tests for: 1) JSON string payload vs parsed object 2) pydantic model return 3) sync + async parity. We had a regression last year when model returned JSON-string.

toni: working on a small PR: reorder checks + add `if isinstance(x, Mapping): return x` early. Adding unit tests in tests/unit/test_parse.py and a functional async test in tests/functional/test_toolcall_async.py.

qa-bot: CI started for branch fix/struct-normalize (job #1201) :white_check_mark:

samir: after local patch I verified rc wheel (0.9.5rc1) and both clients return dict. thanks!

leah: can we include an inline comment in the parser explaining why Mapping must be prioritized to avoid future churn? Also ensure compatibility for python <3.10 import paths for collections.abc.

toni: added comment and try/except import. pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4620 (contains tests).
